newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's exiled king returns home, troops deploy. [CORRECTED 08:50 GMT 13/4]
newsitem.headline: Albania's exiled king returns home, troops deploy. [CORRECTED 08:50 GMT 13/4]

text.p: Albania's King Leka I returned from exile to a chaotic welcome on Saturday as advance troops from a multinational security force deployed in the volatile Balkan state.
King Leka I was thronged by more than 1,000 supporters on his arrival from South Africa by private plane, witnesses said.

Dozens of people broke through police cordons and jumped onto his limousine as he was driven under escort from Rinas airport to the capital. Many supporters chanted "Long Live King Leka" and waved red-and-black Albanian flags.
King Leka, 58, tall and bespectacled, checked into a luxury hotel in central Tirana, where dozens of supporters welcomed him noisily, shouting "King! King!"
He was only two days old when his father, King Zog, fled the country with his family in 1939.
"We will work together to save and rebuild Albania," he told a small group of supporters in his hotel room.

Albania sank into near-anarchy after the collapse of get-rich-quick investment schemes earlier this year, provoking a wave of popular anger. Local newspapers on Saturday put the death toll from six weeks of unrest at 279.
Before leaving exile in South Africa, Leka said in a statement that he believed his people saw him as father of the nation. He called for a referendum on whether the monarchy should be restored.

"Only a referendum under international supervision will grant the Albanian people ... the means to choose the constitutional form of the regime which would best suit the aspirations of the nation, a parliamentary monarchy or a republic," the statement said.
"The people's choice will be binding upon us," it added.
The king said he was returning to Albania to share the difficulties and suffering of his subjects and "to revive your aspirations for the future".
In Rome, a government spokesman said Prime Minister Romano Prodi would go to Albania on Sunday (corrects from Monday) as Italy prepares to head a multinational security mission.

He said Prodi would make a one-day visit to Tirana but gave no further details. Prodi said on Saturday Italy would begin deploying the bulk of its 2,500 troops at the head of the 6,000-strong multinational force to Albania from next Tuesday.
The force will protect distribution of emergency food and medicines.

Some 100 Italian troops had arrived since Friday and most of them were protecting Tirana airport and adapting it for round-the-clock operations, an official source said. A unit of some 20 men arrived in the western port of Durres on Friday.

Small numbers of Spanish, Greek, Turkish and Austrian soldiers had reached Tirana to plot the arrival of the force, military sources and residents said. An advance unit of about 100 French soldiers arrived in the southern Italian port of Brindisi on Friday.

Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta was expected to hold talks with officials in Tirana later on Saturday to discuss the deployment of the force and other bilateral issues, official sources said.
